Player

class Player(id, name, birth_date, observation)[source]

Bases: object

Model for player data.

Attributes:
idint

Unique identifier for the player.

namestr

Name of the player.

birth_datedatetime

Player’s birth date.

observationstr

Additional observations about the player.

PROPERTIESlist[str], class attribute

Field names, filled by initialize_reflexive.

DATA_PROPERTIESlist, class attribute

Field defaults, filled by initialize_reflexive.

Methods

is_valid()

Check whether the player’s data is valid.

set_data(data)

Update the player’s data from a dictionary.

get_data()

Return the player’s data as a one-item list.

Examples

>>> from datetime import datetime
>>> player = Player(1, "John", datetime(2000, 1, 1), "")
>>> player.is_valid()
True
>>> player.get_data()[0]["name"]
'John'

Methods

get_data

Return the field values as a one-item list.

is_valid

Check whether the player's data is valid.

set_data

Update the fields from a dictionary.
is_valid()[source]

Check whether the player’s data is valid.

Returns:
bool

True if the player’s data is valid, False otherwise.

Notes

A player is valid when id is an int, name is not blank, birth_date is not None and no other field (observation) is None.

set_data(data)[source]

Update the fields from a dictionary.

Parameters:
datadict

Values keyed by field name. Keys that are not fields are ignored, and fields missing from data keep their value.

Notes

No validation or type conversion is done.

get_data()[source]

Return the field values as a one-item list.

Returns:
list[dict]

A list with one dictionary that maps each name of PROPERTIES to its current value.
